findings.title: A renamed executable escapes the exec-bit hand-off arm — `drive_handoff_exec_bit` only walks `--diff-filter=A` and `M`, so a candidate that renames a mode-755 file and lands it 644 (filter `R`, and git's diff enables rename detection by default) is classified `candidate` and charges the attempt for a `chmod +x` the implementer may not run

The de-flaked assertions' new wording is covered by no register entry, so criterion (3) is met only for pre-T019 branches — after this merges, a recurrence of L020 under the bounded-wait sentence charges an attempt; the reasoning in `tests/QUARANTINE.md` for not listing them is sound, but the residual is worth stating in the task report

`drive_handoff_stale_pin` still runs on stopped-short rounds — the `cut` veto guards the three early returns, so a 124/137/143 verify falls through to the pin route and builds a release archive that can never contribute a waiver, on the one round that already timed out

`_drive_waived`'s empty-`attributed` branch is unreachable — every call site is guarded by `[ -n "$attr" ]`, so the "this round left no failing line for anything else to explain" wording can never be printed
`drive_implement_envelope` computes `base="$(basename "$f")"` and then `_drive_implement_index "$f"` forks `basename` on the same path a second time, once per envelope per pass
